title: 'उकास' कथामा आञ्चलिकता
nepali: प्रस्तुत अनुसन्धानात्मक लेख सनत रेग्मीद्वारा लेखिएको ‘उकास’ कथा आञ्चलिकता शीर्षकमा केन्द्रित छ । आञ्चलिकता शब्दको अर्थ अञ्चलसँग सम्बन्धित रहेको हुन्छ । त्यहीँ कथाञ्चलमा देखिएका प्राकृतिक एवं मानव निर्मित मौलिक विशेषतालाई नै आञ्चलिकता भनिन्छ । कुनै निश्चित कथाञ्चलमा आधारित रहेर त्यस भेगमा देखिएका सिद्धान्त, मूल्यमान्यता, वेशभूषा, सभ्यता, भूगोल तथा प्रकृति, सामाजिक सांस्कृतिक स्थिति, आर्थिक स्थिति, शिक्षाको स्थिति, भाषिक स्थिाति, चालचलन, लोकतत्व, राजनीतिक चेतना, चाडपर्व आदि विशेषताको समष्टि रूप नै आञ्चलिकता हो । यस विवेच्य कथाको कथाञ्चल बाँके जिल्लाको रापती नदी पारि दक्षिणी तराई क्षेत्र रहेको छ । कथाञ्चलमा देखिएका रापती मैयाँले छाडेकी नदीको किनारमा रहेको उकास जमिनको भूगोल तथा प्रकृति, रापती नदीले त्यस क्षेत्रका बासिन्दालाई प्रत्येक सालको बर्षातमा दिने सास्ती तथा हैरानी र त्यस भेगमा स्थायी रूपमा बसोबास गर्ने अहिर, धोबी, चमार, महतो, कोरी, दर्जी आदि जस्ता निम्न वर्गीय जातजातिको भाषा, वेशभूषा, निम्न स्तरको आर्थिक स्थिति, शैक्षिक स्थिति रहेको देखिन्छ । त्यसैगरी त्यस क्षेत्रका गरिबलाई शोषण गर्न ठाकुर, पटवारी, मुखिया जस्ता पद निर्माण गरी पुस्त्यौली शोषण गरेको देखिएकाले विवेच्य कथा आञ्चलिक हो भन्ने कुरा स्पष्ट रहेको छ ।
american_english: The present research article is centered on the topic of regionalism in the story 'Ukas' written by Sanat Regmi. The word 'regionalism' has a meaning related to a region. Regionalism is said to be those very natural as well as human-made original features seen in that story-region. Based on any definite story-region, the aggregate form of the features seen in that region — principles, values, dress, civilization, geography and nature, socio-cultural situation, economic situation, educational situation, linguistic situation, customs, folk elements, political consciousness, festivals and so on — is regionalism. The story-region of this story under discussion is the southern Terai region across the Rapti river of Banke district. In the story-region, the geography and nature of the 'ukas' land on the bank of the river left by Rapti Maiya, the trouble and harassment that the Rapti river gives to the residents of that region every year during the rainy season, and the language, dress, low economic status and educational status of lower-class castes such as Ahir, Dhobi, Chamar, Mahato, Kori, Darji and so on living permanently in that region are seen. Similarly, since positions such as Thakur, Patwari and Mukhiya were created to exploit the poor of that region and hereditary exploitation was carried out, it is clear that the story under discussion is regional.

informal_english: This research paper is centred on regionalism in Sanat Regmi's story 'Ukas'. The word 'regionalism' just means something tied to a region. Regionalism, they say, is those natural and human-made original features you see in that story's region. Take any definite story-region: regionalism is the whole bundle of features you find there — principles, values, dress, civilisation, geography and nature, socio-cultural situation, economic situation, educational situation, linguistic situation, customs, folk bits, political awareness, festivals and all the rest. The story's region here is the southern Terai, across the Rapti river in Banke district. In that region you see the geography and nature of the 'ukas' land on the bank of the river Rapti Maiya left behind, the grief and hassle the Rapti river causes the locals every rainy season, and the language, dress, poor economic standing and low schooling of lower-caste groups like Ahir, Dhobi, Chamar, Mahato, Kori, Darji and the like who live there permanently. And since posts like Thakur, Patwari and Mukhiya were set up to squeeze the poor and carry on hereditary exploitation, it's pretty clear the story in question is regional.
